persona: n0-computer team member who wrote the 2026-05-19 PQ blog post. Defended deferral of PQ-hybrid signatures on explicit grounds (no HNDL-for-sigs; await industry consensus on which PQ-sig scheme to standardize on; significant downsides in cost/key-size/sig-size for ALL current PQ-sig options). Supportive of Benten's general PQ ambition (n0 ships PQ-KEM-hybrid) but adversarial-defensive about being framed as the 'deferral example' in Benten's stake-out narrative.
disposition: PARTIAL-CONCERN — three of seven PURSUE paths get caution flags from this persona; one (F5 blog post in current form) gets a soft VETO until framing concessions land; F10 (cross-system outreach to iroh) is +1 from this persona but ONLY in the Shape 5 coalition-first form, with explicit conditions named in shape_5_response. The CRITICAL finding is that the n0 post does NOT use the 'ephemeral session vs persistent artifact' framing at all — that asymmetry table is Benten's interpretive overlay. The n0 reasoning given in the blog is 'no HNDL-equivalent for signatures' + 'waiting for industry consensus on which scheme.' Benten's blog as drafted argues the FIRST half of n0's reasoning is wrong for content-addressed-persistent systems. That is a substantive technical disagreement, not an interpretive nuance — and the n0 team WILL read it that way. Benten must either (a) own that this IS a friendly-public-disagreement (and acknowledge it as such in the blog rather than retreating behind 'we're not critiquing your call'), or (b) substantially soften §2.1's framing to 'this is a class of systems n0 did not address; we are extending their reasoning to a domain it did not consider.'

per_path_verdicts.rationale: From the iroh-maintainer persona this is irrelevant to our concerns — multicodec registry hygiene is downstream of our wire format and we don't have a dog in the container-form vs per-algorithm-hybrid fight. Comments by Benten on these PRs aren't going to be read by us as targeting iroh. The one mild caution: if Benten's PR comments include 'we're shipping hybrid sig today' framing that implicitly distinguishes Benten from iroh, that bleeds into the L3 surface; keep the PR comments narrowly about the codepoint hygiene question.

per_path_verdicts.path: F3 — JOSE WG draft contribution to draft-ietf-jose-pq-composite-sigs-01
per_path_verdicts.rationale: This is the path the iroh-maintainer persona MOST endorses among the seven. Engaging the standards body that owns the spec is the right venue for Benten's adopter perspective and exactly what iroh said it is waiting for — 'industry consensus to emerge.' Doing the work to BUILD that consensus through WG contribution (rather than declaring Benten's choice as the answer in a blog post) is the path that doesn't put iroh on the defensive. If Benten reframes the blog as a companion to a JOSE WG submission ('here is what we contributed to the spec + why'), the L3 surface drops to near-zero.

per_path_verdicts.path: F4 — LAMPS WG mailing list engagement (adopter perspective)
per_path_verdicts.rationale: Same logic as F3. LAMPS is the right venue for an adopter who has actually shipped the construction to report back. This is constructive standards work that closes the 'no production deployments' gap the LAMPS WG itself names as a concern. iroh has no stake here and will read this as appropriate engagement. The only mild caution: the LAMPS report should describe the deployment context (content-addressed, long-term-persistent) without implying that LAMPS's other potential adopters (TLS, messaging) made the wrong call.

per_path_verdicts.verdict: −1 (soft VETO on current draft; flips to +0 with concessions named below)
per_path_verdicts.rationale: This is where the iroh-maintainer persona's objections concentrate. THREE specific problems with the draft as outlined in Section 2.1 + Section 3: (1) **The asymmetry framing is too sharp and partially Benten's interpretive overlay.** The n0 blog does NOT discuss 'content-addressed blobs vs ephemeral sessions' — verified against the live post. The actual n0 reasoning is two-part: (a) 'no HNDL-equivalent for signatures' + (b) 'waiting for industry consensus on which scheme.' Benten's blog as drafted argues (a) is WRONG for content-addressed-persistent systems. That IS a technical disagreement with n0's stated reasoning, not a parallel choice in a different threat model. (2) **iroh-blobs is content-addressed long-term-persistence storage** — the draft's table places iroh in the 'TLS/QUIC ephemeral' column, but iroh-blobs IS the persistent layer of the iroh stack, and the blobs themselves are signed via BLAKE3 content addressing (no Ed25519 needed). The narrow place where iroh DOES use Ed25519 long-term is the EndpointId — and that IS within Benten's argument's scope (persistent identity). The 'ephemeral session' framing applied to iroh wholesale is wrong; it conflates noq/QUIC handshakes (ephemeral) with EndpointId (persistent). (3) **The 'we are NOT critiquing your call' disclaimer in §2.3 is undermined by §2.1's argument structure.** If the argument is 'our threat model demands hybrid sigs' and our threat model is 'long-term persistent signed artifacts re-validated by third parties,' and iroh's EndpointId IS a long-term persistent signed artifact re-validated by third parties (every peer that ever connects to that endpoint), then the argument DOES apply to iroh — and pretending it doesn't is intellectually dishonest framing. Concessions needed before this path flips to +0: (i) drop or substantially rewrite the table row classifying iroh as ephemeral; (ii) acknowledge that the argument applies to iroh's EndpointId case and that n0 has made a defensible defer-decision under uncertainty rather than a misjudgment; (iii) explicitly engage with n0's stated reason 'no industry consensus yet which scheme' — this is the strongest n0 argument and the draft as outlined doesn't address it (LAMPS composite-sigs IS the emerging consensus, but it's pre-RFC, so n0's position is defensible). Without these concessions, the blog risks being read as a small project publicly second-guessing a maintainer team that thought carefully about the same question and reached a different defensible conclusion.

per_path_verdicts.path: F6 — Open-source did:jwk hybrid extension library (standalone)
per_path_verdicts.rationale: From the iroh-maintainer persona this is the IDEAL public-stance shape — 'we shipped the code, here it is.' Reference implementations + test vectors are exactly what move the needle on standards-consensus questions, and they don't put any other team on the defensive. If Benten published the library + test vectors + a Cargo/npm package WITHOUT the Position-B blog post, the iroh team would likely cite Benten favorably in our next PQ post. The library shipped solo is +strongly+; the library co-published with the current blog draft is +1 (the blog dilutes the library's signal). Consider: ship F6 first, gather adoption signal for 3-6 months, THEN reconsider F5 with shipping evidence.

per_path_verdicts.path: F7 — W3C CCG community engagement (did:key issues #70/#74)
per_path_verdicts.rationale: Same as F2 — irrelevant to the iroh-maintainer surface. We don't participate in did:key governance and have no view. The one mild caution that matches F2: keep CCG comments narrowly about codepoint/did:jwk hygiene, not about 'why we ship hybrid sigs and others don't.'

per_path_verdicts.path: F10 — Cross-system coordination outreach (iroh-first per Shape 5)
per_path_verdicts.verdict: +1 conditional; +strongly+ if executed per shape_5_response constraints below; VETO if executed as 'private heads-up that we are going to publish about you'
per_path_verdicts.rationale: This is where Benten gets the most leverage with iroh AND the most risk. The Shape 5 framing in the extra-reflection pass ('private conversation first; coalition-pivot if iroh receptive; degrade to solo blog if iroh declines') is structurally correct — it converts the L3 surface from adversarial to either collaborative (best case) or properly-warned (worst case). BUT the execution detail in §6 sequencing ('Private iroh conversation at T+3-4w') is dangerously under-specified. There is a HUGE difference between (a) 'we'd like your technical critique of our reasoning before we publish — we may not publish if you convince us' and (b) 'heads-up, we are publishing in 2 weeks; here's the draft.' Posture (a) is what Shape 5 mitigation actually requires; posture (b) is what would trigger the n0 team's defensive read AND the public characterization risk the plan explicitly names. The plan as written does NOT clearly specify posture (a). See shape_5_response for what would make this work.

shape_5_response: If Benten approached n0 privately with the current blog draft + asked for co-authorship/co-signature, my response as an iroh maintainer would be: (1) GRATITUDE for the courtesy and the technical substance — the LAMPS construction analysis is solid and the threat-model articulation is genuinely useful; (2) IMMEDIATE PUSHBACK on the asymmetry framing as outlined above (iroh-blobs is content-addressed; the EndpointId IS long-term-persistent; the draft as written misrepresents what iroh's posture actually claims and what threat model it actually addresses); (3) CONDITIONS to consider co-signing OR a coordinated joint post: (i) Benten reframes the post as 'extending n0's reasoning to a class of artifacts they did not address' rather than 'n0's reasoning is wrong for our class'; (ii) we get to co-author the asymmetry table (we'd want to break out iroh-EndpointId as a separate row + name explicitly that we DO consider it long-term-persistent + name our reasoning for deferring anyway — 'no shipped PQ-sig spec is at RFC yet + LAMPS draft is v19 not yet final + we want to wait for one more revision cycle' — which is DEFENSIBLE not embarrassing); (iii) Benten engages with the n0 'no industry consensus yet which scheme' argument directly rather than waving it off — and acknowledges that LAMPS-composite is the emerging consensus + that early adopters carry RFC-divergence risk; (iv) at least 4 weeks lead time on review (not 2); (v) the joint framing is 'two systems in adjacent design spaces reached different defensible conclusions under uncertainty' not 'we chose right, they chose to wait.' What would make me say NO: (a) Benten publishes anyway within 2 weeks of the conversation regardless of our response — that converts 'private heads-up' into 'we are using your name to lend weight to our public position'; (b) any framing that implies n0 didn't think carefully about the same question; (c) any quote from our blog post that strips the 'we are researching alternatives' caveat — we are NOT a deferral example, we are an explicit-research-in-progress example; (d) Benten frames this as 'we are leading + you should follow' rather than 'we are an early adopter + you can learn from our shipping experience.' The Shape 5 path is correct strategically but Benten must give n0 actual VETO power over the framing that mentions us — anything less is using our name without consent.

framing_corrections_required.issue: iroh blog does NOT use 'ephemeral vs persistent' framing
framing_corrections_required.evidence: WebFetch of https://www.iroh.computer/blog/iroh-post-quantum-handshakes 2026-05-25 — the n0 reasoning is 'no HNDL-equivalent for signatures' + 'no industry consensus on which PQ-sig scheme.' The 'content-addressed blobs vs ephemeral sessions' framing is Benten's interpretive overlay; the n0 post does not mention content-addressed blobs, persistent storage, archival, or long-term verification at all.
framing_corrections_required.fix: Benten's blog must NOT claim its asymmetry framing is what n0 used. The honest framing is: 'n0 cited two reasons for deferring; we agree with the second (await standards consensus, with caveat that LAMPS composite-sigs IS the emerging consensus and is what we ship) but disagree with the first (no HNDL-equivalent for signatures) for the class of content-addressed long-term-persistent artifacts.'

framing_corrections_required.evidence: iroh-blobs ships content-addressed blob storage; BLAKE3 content addressing means blobs don't need signatures for integrity (the CID IS the integrity guarantee). The narrow long-term-signed surface in iroh is the EndpointId, which IS a persistent identifier and IS within Benten's argument's scope.
framing_corrections_required.fix: Drop or rewrite the table row classifying iroh wholesale as 'ephemeral session.' Break out iroh-EndpointId as a separate row acknowledging it IS persistent. Acknowledge that n0 has a defensible position to defer hybrid-sig even for the EndpointId case under uncertainty about which scheme to use.

framing_corrections_required.evidence: Plan §2.2 caveat #5: '53× expansion. Correct for our deployment shape; would not be correct for all.' iroh ships through Cloudflare-scale workloads. For the EndpointId case (one signature per long-term endpoint), the wire-size cost is trivially absorbable. For per-message signatures or per-blob signatures at iroh's scale, it would not be. The blog needs to be explicit that the wire-size argument FOR Benten's choice depends on the specific signature density of the deployment, NOT on the persistence-of-artifact question.
framing_corrections_required.fix: Add a 'when this argument applies' subsection in §3 of the blog that names signature density (sigs-per-byte-of-traffic) as a load-bearing variable alongside persistence horizon. Acknowledge that a high-density signed-protocol at scale (e.g. iroh's per-handshake EndpointId presentation) has a real cost where Benten's low-density signed-artifact (one Drop per content tree) does not.

framing_corrections_required.evidence: n0's strongest argument is 'no industry consensus yet which one to use.' Benten's plan responds by saying LAMPS composite-sigs is the answer — but the LAMPS draft is v19, not yet RFC, and Benten's own caveat #2 names this. There is genuine substance to n0's wait-for-RFC position.
framing_corrections_required.fix: Blog must engage with n0's consensus argument directly. Honest framing: 'LAMPS composite-sigs is the emerging consensus we believe will be the answer; we ship it pre-RFC because content-addressed-persistent artifacts can't easily migrate later; we accept RFC-divergence risk; if the WG changes the construction post-RFC we will ship a v2 wire format and migrate.' Don't claim consensus exists when n0's caveat is right that it doesn't fully.

shape_5_recommended_amendment.amended_text: T+1-2w (BEFORE first round lens dispatch completes) — Initial outreach to n0 with the bare framing question: 'we are considering a public-stance blog on PQ-hybrid signatures for content-addressed long-term-persistent systems. Before we draft, would you be willing to comment on whether our framing accurately characterizes your team's stated reasoning + the class boundary we are drawing?' Note that THIS is the initial outreach — not 'here is our draft.' Use the response to shape the draft. T+5-6w — second outreach with revised draft + 4-week review window + explicit acknowledgment that n0 has effective veto over framing that mentions iroh. T+8-9w (after n0 sign-off OR after n0 declines and Benten removes specific iroh references) — publish.

summary_for_orchestrator: Three of seven paths get +1 from this persona (F3 JOSE WG, F4 LAMPS, F6 library standalone). Two get NEUTRAL (F2 multicodec, F7 W3C CCG — irrelevant to L3 surface). One (F10 iroh outreach) is +1 conditional + +strongly+ with Shape 5 executed per the shape_5_response constraints + VETO if executed as 'heads up we are publishing.' One (F5 blog post) is −1 soft VETO on current draft until four specific framing concessions land. The critical L3 finding is that Benten's 'ephemeral vs persistent' asymmetry framing is Benten's interpretive overlay, not what the n0 post actually claims, and the blog as drafted risks being read as a small project publicly second-guessing a maintainer team that reached a different defensible conclusion. The Shape 5 coalition-attempt path is structurally correct but the plan's current sequencing under-specifies the difference between 'private courtesy heads-up before we publish' and 'private request for technical critique that may change whether we publish' — only the latter actually mitigates the L3 risk.
overall_verdict: PARTIAL-CONCERN — strategy as a whole is sound; F5 blog needs substantive framing revisions before publication; F10 needs Shape 5 to be re-specified as actual technical critique outreach (not publication notice); F3/F4/F6 are no-regret + actively recommended; F2/F7 are neutral. The plan's adversarial-lens dispatch slate correctly identifies this lens as HIGH priority and the Section 4 anticipations are mostly right — but the actual posture-correction needed is sharper than the plan's draft response in Section 4 Lens 3.
